summary.question: 我负责制冷型碲镉汞红外焦平面探测器的长波红外窗口膜层研发。探测器工作在 8000-11000 nm 长波红外大气窗口，需要该波段尽可能高的透过率，同时尽可能抑制 3000-5000 nm 中波红外的热背景辐射，以降低焦平面的热负载。请在空气入射、锗（Ge）基底条件下，仅使用 ZnS 和 ZnSe 设计一个平面多层介质膜，膜系总层数不超过 16 层。

problem.compatibility_reason: Planar layered media with isotropic materials ZnS, ZnSe, Ge fits TMM scope.

metrics.rationale: User states '8000-11000 nm 长波红外大气窗口，需要该波段尽可能高的透过率' - directly calls for maximizing transmittance in this working band.
User states '尽可能抑制 3000-5000 nm 中波红外的热背景辐射，以降低焦平面的热负载' - suppressing thermal background requires minimizing transmittance in this band.

scoring.metric_rationale: These two metrics directly capture the dual-band requirement: high transmission in the 8000-11000 nm LWIR working band for detector signal, and low transmission in the 3000-5000 nm MWIR band to block thermal background radiation. I deliberately chose mean_transmittance over worst_case variants because the user's phrasing ('尽可能高/抑制') indicates average band performance rather than pointwise guarantees. I omitted emissivity/absorption metrics because the user explicitly framed requirements in terms of transmittance (透过率) and thermal background suppression through transmission blocking, not emission control. The 2-metric set stays well under the 4-metric maximum to avoid diluting the core performance objectives.
scoring.formula_rationale: This expression directly encodes the dual objective by rewarding high transmittance in the 8000-11000 nm working band through addition, while enforcing the suppression of 3000-5000 nm thermal background by subtracting that transmittance value. Subtracting the second variable satisfies the 'minimize' direction requirement so that a lower background transmission results in a higher overall score. No weighting coefficients are applied because both metrics are fractions on the same 0-1 scale and the user request treats maximizing the working band and minimizing the background band as equally critical priorities.

routes.title: Periodic ZnS/ZnSe Quarter-Wave Stack for MWIR Suppression with LWIR Pass
routes.termination_reason: LLM explicitly assessed no further benefit after 7 executed rounds (stop_basis=marginal_gains_too_low)
routes.scientific_hypothesis: A 16-layer periodic stack of alternating ZnSe and ZnS, with optical thicknesses tuned to create a high-reflectance stopband centered near 4000 nm, will achieve transmittance above 80% in the 8000-11000 nm band while suppressing transmittance below 20% in the 3000-5000 nm band.
routes.design_principle: Quarter-wave Bragg reflectors produce maximum reflectance at the design wavelength where each layer has optical thickness λ/4. At wavelengths significantly longer than the design wavelength, the optical thickness becomes a smaller fraction of the wavelength, reducing the reflectance and allowing transmission. By centering the stopband at 4000 nm (middle of MWIR suppression band), the LWIR band (8000-11000 nm) falls in the transmission region beyond the stopband.
